A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same CURE research paper, with 28 readable pages including Appendices A–C. Text, equations, tables, and figures support a complete comparison; differences are limited to version metadata and small presentation adjustments.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original coding and unit-test generation experiments, benchmark accuracies, API-model comparisons, and ablations. Appendix B reports standard errors and response lengths.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the original experimental results, including benchmark evaluations, ablations, statistical reporting, and response-length measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same coder–unit tester co-evolution procedure, execution-based rewards, reinforcement-learning objective, and response-length reward transformation.

E1.justification: Both versions use LiveBench, MBPP, LiveCodeBench, CodeContests, and CodeForces. Coverage of coding, unit-test generation, test-time scaling, agentic applications, and generated-test supervision is unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same Qwen, DeepSeek-Coder, Seed-Coder, and GPT comparators. Figure 6 also retains the same agentic-method comparisons and optimization/reward alternatives.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix C retain the same splits, preprocessing, model sizes, training schedules, metrics, and agentic evaluation procedures. Table 1 still evaluates BoN using 16 code solutions and 16 generated tests.

E4.justification: The sampling-budget analyses in Figures 4–5, optimization and reward ablations in Figure 6(b), and generated-test examples in Appendix C.5 are unchanged. No robustness analysis or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Appendix B, Table 3 retains standard errors and the statement that unit-test and code accuracies use 16 independent runs, while BoN uses one run per benchmark. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Reported results in Tables 1–4, Figures 1–7, and the appendix examples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports the same ReasonFlux-Coder-14B LiveBench UT/Code/BoN accuracies of 73.3%, 47.5%, and 60.2% in both versions.

T1.justification: The reward-precision definition, Theorem 3.1, Proposition A.1, and the proofs and reward derivation in Appendix A are unchanged. No mathematical assumption or argument is revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same claims about co-evolution without ground-truth code supervision, improved coding and unit testing, long-CoT efficiency, downstream applications, and use as a reinforcement-learning reward model.

C2.justification: Interpretations of reward design, smaller gains for long-CoT models, and downstream utility remain unchanged. Section 3.1 retains the qualifications concerning inaccurate tests, ambiguous problems, and binary outputs; Section 5 retains the same future direction.

D1.justification: Training hyperparameters, eight-A100 hardware disclosure, prompts, data-conversion instructions, and agentic implementation details remain unchanged in Section 4.1.2 and Appendix C. Code and model-access links also remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Both versions contain the same 54 references and related-work discussion. Positioning relative to O1-Coder, UTGEN, earlier unit-test generation methods, and reinforcement-learning approaches is unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1, 3 June 2025, to v2, 25 September 2025. The title, authors, scientific prose, terminology, and section and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 and its caption shift upward by approximately 1.8 points, alongside the updated marginal version stamp. Figure and table contents, designs, numbering, and the remaining page organization are retained.

improvement.justification: The main text and Appendices A–C retain the same scientific content, evidence, theory, and reproducibility information. Updated version metadata and tiny layout adjustments do not meaningfully improve or diminish the paper's quality.
